Surmamon Nongbri & ors vs State of Meghalaya & ors
 Coram:
 Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sanjib Banerjee, Chief Justice
 Hon'ble Mr. Justice W. Diengdoh, Judge
 Appearance:
 For the Appellants : Mr H.L. Shangreiso, Sr Adv. with
 Mr P.K. Shaki, Adv.
 Mr T. Dkhar, Adv.
 For the Respondents : Mr N.D. Chullai, Aag with
Mr A.H. Kharwanlang, Addl Sr Ga Ms R. Colney, Ga The appeal is directed against a judgment and
order of May 2, 2023 passed in the second round of writ proceedings, so to say, between the present
appellants and the State.

2. The matter in issue is whether the appellants' parcels of land have been, in effect, taken
possession of by the State following the building of a dam and the alleged submergence of such land
within the waterbody that has been artificially created upon the construction of the dam.

3.  By the order impugned, certain directions have been issued, inter alia, for the Public Health Engineering Department of the State to conduct a fresh survey and identify whether the lands of the appellants remain submerged after 2011 and till date and, if the lands are found to be submerged,
initiate the process for acquisition of such lands that remain submerged.

entities.text: Public Health Engineering Department of the State
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The further direction issued is that if the survey reveals otherwise, that only during some part of 2011 portions of the land had been submerged but the submergence has not occurred since, then the previous money allocated towards damages to be paid to the appellants must be disbursed.

4. According to the appellants, the previous round of litigation culminated in a direction being issued by a Division Bench of this Court requiring the Chief Secretary to the State to look into the matter and to take a reasoned decision thereon.

The appellants assert that the Chief Secretary's report in such regard was published on or about March 13, 2017 and it provided for compensation in excess of Rs. 6.64 crore to the apparent land-losers.

The appellants submit that by such time the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 stood substituted by the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: What the appellants insinuate is that in view of the Act of 2013, the mode of assessing compensation stood altered and the methodology adopted by the Chief Secretary in his report of March 13, 2017 would not pass muster under the provisions for larger compensation introduced by the Act of 2013.

The appellants claim that the PHE apparently requested the LA Collector to waive the provisions of the 2013 Act so that the compensation as indicated in the Chief Secretary's report could be disbursed, whereupon the LA Collector, quite appropriately, responded that he had no authority to waive the applicability of any provision of law.
6. What also remains the undisputed position is that no notification was issued under the Act of 1894 despite a draft notification in such regard having been prepared by the State.
The real controversy is as to whether parcels of land belonging to the appellants herein have been lost to the appellants forever or they only remained submerged for some period of time in 2011.

If such lands continue to remain submerged periodically ever since the construction of the dam, it would tantamount to the appellants having lost their land and the State having, de facto, taken possession thereof otherwise than by the procedure established by law.

7. Accordingly, the State is directed to immediately ensure that photographs of the entire area,
including of the parcels of land claimed by the appellants, are immediately taken by drones to establish the present position.
Such drone photography must be conducted upon notice to the appellants herein.
If reasonable notice of at least two days is given to the appellants, it will be open to the appellants to depute one or more representatives to be present at the time that the photographs are taken.
8. It is also necessary that the survey directed to be conducted by the order impugned should be completed as expeditiously as possible and, preferably, within six weeks from date.
The completion of the survey in terms of the order impugned will be without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the appellants.

9. The matter will appear a fortnight hence for the photographs to be received; whereupon, if immediate further directions are not required to be issued, it will appear seven weeks hence, after the completion of the survey.
The revenue records revealing the plots must be produced at the final hearing.

10. List on June 28, 2023.
 (W. Diengdoh) (Sanjib Banerjee)
 Judge Chief Justice Meghalaya 06.06.2023 "Sylvana PS"
